transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I've developed an intense, overwhelming fear of elevators and enclosed spaces. It has gotten so bad that it's making my daily life really difficult to manage.
Is this intense fear and anxiety strictly limited to elevators and enclosed spaces, or do you find yourself constantly worrying about many other different areas of your life as well?
It is strictly limited to elevators and tight, enclosed spaces. I don't really worry about other areas of my life in general. It's just those specific situations that trigger this intense fear.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ['Specific Phobia', 'Generalized Anxiety Disorder']. Based on this conversation, Generalized Anxiety Disorder is ruled out because the patient explicitly states that their anxiety is strictly limited to elevators and enclosed spaces and they do not experience generalized, pervasive worry about other areas of life. Therefore, the diagnosis is narrowed down to Specific Phobia.
